pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasound finding of a mature ovarian teratoma containing neural tissue combined with an EEG showing extreme delta brush pattern PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis is a severe autoimmune encephalitis mediated by IgG autoantibodies against the GluN1 subunit of the NMDA receptor. In young female patients, it is frequently a paraneoplastic syndrome triggered by a mature ovarian teratoma (dermoid cyst) containing ectopic neural tissue. The immune system generates antibodies against the ectopic neural NMDA receptors, which cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to neuronal NMDA receptors, causing receptor cross-linking and internalisation. This selective loss of NMDA receptor function disrupts frontostriatal networks, triggering progressive psychosis, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, and central respiratory failure. Removal of the teratoma combined with immunotherapy leads to full or substantial recovery in the majority of patients.
